sentences.en: In the Tempelhof Schoenenberg district of Berlin, there's an enormous concrete structure that sits across the street from a supermarket.
sentences.zh: 在柏林的滕珀尔霍夫-舍内贝格区，有一座巨大的混凝土建筑，它坐落在一家超市的马路对面。

sentences.en: It's obscured by trees, surrounded by residential apartments, and gently flecked with German graffiti.
sentences.zh: 它被树木遮挡，周围环绕着居民公寓，上面零星点缀着德国涂鸦。

sentences.en: I am quite possibly the most jet-lagged I've ever been in my entire life.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子可能从没像现在这样时差反应严重。

sentences.en: And I'm waiting for my Uber.
Or as they say here in Germany, my Uba.
sentences.zh: 或者像德国人说的那样，等我的“乌巴”（Uba）。

sentences.en: We sent 99PI producer Vivian Leigh there to check it out.
sentences.zh: 我们派了《99%隐形》的制作人薇薇安·李去那里一探究竟。

sentences.en: Jet-lag be damned, I met up with Hannah Fischer and Vincent Brookman.
sentences.zh: 不管时差了，我见到了汉娜·费舍尔和文森特·布鲁克曼。

sentences.en: Hannah is the curator and deputy director for the Tempelhof Schoenenberg Museums, and Vincent is a journalist and tour guide.
sentences.zh: 汉娜是滕珀尔霍夫-舍内贝格博物馆的馆长兼副主任，文森特是一位记者兼导游。

sentences.en: They were there to show me around a curious neighborhood landmark.
sentences.zh: 他们带我参观了这个奇特的街区地标。

sentences.en: From afar, it kind of looks like a derelict, brutalist grain silo.
sentences.zh: 从远处看，它看起来就像一个废弃的粗野主义风格的谷仓。

sentences.en: Is it a popular site for people to visit, this one?
sentences.zh: 这是一个热门的旅游景点吗？

sentences.en: For example, Schoenenberg, it's the most popular.
sentences.zh: 比如在舍内贝格，它是最受欢迎的。

sentences.en: And it is the least aesthetically pleasing.
sentences.zh: 而且它也是最不美观的。

sentences.en: This structure is a bit hard to describe because there's literally nothing else like it in the world.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑有点难以描述，因为世界上真的没有其他类似的东西。

sentences.en: On the surface, it's a very, very big, very, very heavy cylindrical block of solid concrete about the height of a four-story building.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，它是一个非常非常巨大、非常非常沉重的圆柱形实心混凝土块，大约有四层楼高。

sentences.en: This concrete, 12,650, I think, tons of concrete.
sentences.zh: 这块混凝土，我想大约有12650吨重。

sentences.en: And sitting underneath those 12,650 tons of concrete is a narrow chamber about eight feet in diameter that descends 60 feet into the ground.
sentences.zh: 在那12650吨混凝土下方，是一个直径约八英尺的狭窄竖井，向下延伸了60英尺深。

sentences.en: There's a ladder here that we can't use now, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 这里有个梯子，可惜我们现在不能用。

sentences.en: And then it goes, I think, 18 meters into the ground.
sentences.zh: 然后它向下延伸，我想大概有18米深。

sentences.en: Have you guys ever crawled down there?
This entire structure was designed to test the soil in this area of Berlin.
sentences.zh: 整个建筑的设计初衷是为了测试柏林这一带的土壤。

sentences.en: That chamber was once an observation area where researchers measured how the soil below was responding to the pressure exerted by the weight of the cylinder on top of it.
sentences.zh: 那个竖井曾经是一个观测区，研究人员在那里测量下方的土壤如何应对上方圆柱体重量所施加的压力。

sentences.en: Whether the cylinder itself was shifting, sinking into the ground, exciting stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 比如圆柱体本身是否在位移、是否在下沉，诸如此类令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: People from all over the world come to Berlin to see what is essentially an abandoned soil testing research tool.
sentences.zh: 来自世界各地的人们来到柏林，就是为了看这个本质上已经废弃的土壤测试研究工具。

sentences.en: And the name of this unusual tourist site is just about as easy to pronounce as it is to describe.
sentences.zh: 而这个不同寻常的旅游景点的名字，和它的外形一样难以描述，也同样难以发音。

sentences.en: And in English, then it's the heavy load bearing body.
sentences.zh: 翻译成英语就是“重载承重体”。

sentences.en: Does it make sense in English even?
The Schwerbelastungskörper is kind of a tongue twister.
But luckily, there's a few other simpler nicknames for it.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，它还有几个更简单的绰号。

sentences.en: The cylinder, the concrete cylinder, the concrete mushroom, because it sort of looks like a mushroom.
sentences.zh: 圆柱体、混凝土圆柱体、混凝土蘑菇，因为它看起来有点像蘑菇。

sentences.en: But locals in the area have referred to it by a much more nefarious nickname.
sentences.zh: 但当地人给它起了一个更邪恶的绰号。

sentences.en: It used to be the nickname Nazi klotz.
sentences.zh: 它曾经被称为“纳粹块”（Nazi klotz）。

sentences.en: A klotz is like a heavy kind of stone that you put onto something.
sentences.zh: “Klotz”指的是那种压在某物上的沉重石块。

sentences.en: And Nazi, so it's kind of like Nazi block.
sentences.zh: 再加上“纳粹”，所以就像是“纳粹块”。

sentences.en: The Schwerbelastungskörper is not famous for what it does, but who built it.
sentences.zh: “Schwerbelastungskörper”出名不是因为它的功能，而是因为建造它的人。

sentences.en: This big, crumbling piece of concrete was actually the first step in a monstrous urban planning scheme dreamed up by Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 这块巨大的、正在崩塌的混凝土，实际上是阿道夫·希特勒构想的一项骇人听闻的城市规划方案的第一步。
谢天谢地，那个计划从未实现。

sentences.en: Now, this Nazi block is one of the only remaining monuments to the Third Reich's most colossal architectural failure.
sentences.zh: 现在，这个“纳粹块”是第三帝国最宏大的建筑失败工程中仅存的纪念碑之一。

sentences.en: There was a phrase that leaders in the Third Reich said about architecture.
sentences.zh: 第三帝国的领导人曾有一句关于建筑的格言。

sentences.en: That it was Worte aus Stein, or words in stone.
sentences.zh: 即“石头的语言”（Worte aus Stein）。

sentences.en: It means that architecture has a specific ability to bypass language and reasoning, to have a direct impact on a person's emotions.
sentences.zh: 这意味着建筑有一种特殊的能力，可以绕过语言和理性，直接影响人的情绪。

sentences.en: If you've ever walked into a family friend's farmhouse-style home and immediately felt a sense of coziness,
sentences.zh: 如果你走进朋友家那种农舍风格的房子，立刻感到一种温馨感，

sentences.en: or had your breath taken away while standing at the top of the Empire State Building,
sentences.zh: 或者站在帝国大厦顶端时感到屏息凝神，

sentences.en: then you know exactly what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 那你完全明白我在说什么。

sentences.en: Architecture can move you and shape your actions in ways that you aren't even aware of.
sentences.zh: 建筑可以以你甚至意识不到的方式打动你并塑造你的行为。

sentences.en: Hitler not only understood this innate power about architecture, he weaponized it.
sentences.zh: 希特勒不仅理解建筑这种与生俱来的力量，他还将其武器化了。

sentences.en: When we think about architecture and weaponization, especially around the Third Reich,
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论建筑与武器化时，特别是在第三帝国背景下，

sentences.en: you know, you might think about the Atlantic Wall or bomb shelters.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想到大西洋壁垒或防空洞。

sentences.en: This is Despin Estradigakis, an architectural historian at the University at Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 这是布法罗大学的建筑历史学家德斯平·埃斯特拉迪加基斯。
zh_words: 德斯平·埃斯特拉迪加基斯

sentences.en: But there are a lot of ways in which architecture can be instrumentalized for ideological purposes
sentences.zh: 但建筑在很多方面都可以被工具化以服务于意识形态目的，

sentences.en: that are not maybe as obvious, but that can be very powerful.
sentences.zh: 这些方式可能不那么明显，但却非常强大。

sentences.en: Hitler was infatuated with art and architecture, enough that he was famously rejected from art school a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 希特勒对艺术和建筑非常痴迷，以至于他曾两次被艺术学校拒之门外，这很有名。

sentences.en: Even early on, he spoke openly about the ways architecture and power are intertwined.
sentences.zh: 即使在早期，他也公开谈论过建筑与权力之间交织的方式。

sentences.en: If you look at Mein Kampf, and I hope you won't, but if you want to torture yourself,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看《我的奋斗》，我希望你不会看，但如果你想折磨自己的话，

sentences.en: in Mein Kampf, he writes about the importance of architecture,
sentences.zh: 在《我的奋斗》中，他写到了建筑的重要性，

sentences.en: and particularly the importance of architecture to create the Volksgemeinschaft.
sentences.zh: 特别是建筑对于创造“人民共同体”（Volksgemeinschaft）的重要性。

sentences.en: And the Volksgemeinschaft is this absolutely central concept in National Socialism.
sentences.zh: “人民共同体”是国家社会主义中绝对核心的概念。

sentences.en: It is the racially unified community.
sentences.zh: 它指的是种族统一的共同体。

sentences.en: The Volksgemeinschaft literally translates to people's community.
sentences.zh: “Volksgemeinschaft”字面翻译就是“人民的共同体”。

sentences.en: And the concept was central to Hitler's racist and anti-Semitic ideology.
sentences.zh: 这个概念是希特勒种族主义和反犹太主义意识形态的核心。

sentences.en: It claimed that there was a, quote, racial hierarchy, which there isn't,
sentences.zh: 它声称存在一种所谓的“种族等级制度”（其实并不存在），

sentences.en: and a, quote, ideal way of German life, again, which there isn't.
sentences.zh: 以及一种所谓的“理想的德国生活方式”（同样也不存在）。

sentences.en: Look, Hitler was an ahistorical idiot who made a number of false assertions.
sentences.zh: 听着，希特勒是个无视历史的白痴，他提出了许多虚假的断言。

sentences.en: One of them was that the ancient Roman Empire represented the peak of human civilization
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是古罗马帝国代表了人类文明的巅峰，

sentences.en: and that Germans were, quote, racial ancestors of the Romans and therefore at the top of that hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 而德国人是罗马人的所谓“种族祖先”，因此处于等级制度的顶端。

sentences.en: Hitler's looking in particular at ancient Rome, and more specifically at the public buildings,
sentences.zh: 希特勒特别关注古罗马，更具体地说是公共建筑，

sentences.en: the state buildings of ancient Rome, the temples, the baths, the Colosseum.
sentences.zh: 古罗马的国家建筑、神庙、浴场、斗兽场。

sentences.en: And he says that in its great monuments, a culture expresses its most profound values.
sentences.zh: 他说，在一个文化的伟大纪念碑中，表达了它最深刻的价值观。

sentences.en: And also he's thinking about the things that will remain when everything else fades away.
sentences.zh: 而且他还思考着当一切都消逝时，什么会留存下来。

sentences.en: And he says wars come and go, but it is the art and the architecture of a civilization that remains.
sentences.zh: 他说战争来来去去，但留存下来的是一个文明的艺术和建筑。

sentences.en: So he's thinking about this long before he gets into power.
sentences.zh: 所以他在掌权之前很久就开始思考这个问题了。

sentences.en: In 1933, Hitler was appointed chancellor of Germany and finally had the political power he needed to create these monuments.
sentences.zh: 1933年，希特勒被任命为德国总理，终于拥有了创造这些纪念碑所需的政治权力。

sentences.en: He just needed an architect to actually build them.
sentences.zh: 他只需要一位建筑师来真正建造它们。

sentences.en: Could you tell me a little bit about Albert Speer?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲阿尔伯特·斯佩尔吗？

sentences.en: Like how did, I know it's...
sentences.zh: 比如他是怎么……我知道这是……

sentences.en: How many, how many hours would you like?
This is Magnus Brechtgen, deputy director of the Institute for Contemporary History in Munich.
sentences.zh: 这是慕尼黑当代历史研究所副所长马格努斯·布雷希特根。

sentences.en: Albert Speer was a highly ambitious young architect.
sentences.zh: 阿尔伯特·斯佩尔是一位非常有野心的年轻建筑师。

sentences.en: He was the son of an architect.
His father made a lot of money.
His mother had a lot of money.
So Albert Speer was completely financially independent.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔伯特·斯佩尔在经济上完全独立。

sentences.en: He could do whatever he wanted.
sentences.zh: 他可以做任何他想做的事。

sentences.en: And what he wanted was the resources and backing of the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 而他想要的是纳粹党的资源和支持。

sentences.en: Speer was sufficiently talented as an architect, but it was his charm and ruthless ambition that landed him in Hitler's orbit.
sentences.zh: 斯佩尔作为建筑师很有才华，但正是他的魅力和冷酷的野心让他进入了希特勒的圈子。

sentences.en: Albert Speer would magically appear whenever Hitler was coming to do a tour of the construction site.
sentences.zh: 每当希特勒来视察工地时，阿尔伯特·斯佩尔总会神奇地出现。

sentences.en: You know, a few minutes beforehand, there was Speer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，提前几分钟，斯佩尔就在那儿了。

sentences.en: And he would join, you know, the architects and the patron and they would walk around the site.
sentences.zh: 他会加入建筑师和赞助人的行列，一起在工地上走动。

sentences.en: And, you know, the workmen would just kind of make jokes about this, this young hanger-on.
sentences.zh: 工人们经常拿这个年轻的“跟屁虫”开玩笑。

sentences.en: But Speer was there to learn.
sentences.zh: 但斯佩尔去那里是为了学习。

sentences.en: Like he was there to learn and to figure out what it was that Hitler wanted, what he liked, what he didn't like, and to be noticed.
sentences.zh: 他去那里是为了学习并弄清楚希特勒想要什么、喜欢什么、不喜欢什么，并引起注意。

sentences.en: Speer was still a relatively young man when he had a streak of good luck.
sentences.zh: 斯佩尔还很年轻时就走了一次好运。

sentences.en: Hitler's top architect suddenly dropped dead.
sentences.zh: 希特勒的首席建筑师突然去世了。

sentences.en: At 28 years old, Speer was launched into the position of chief architect for the Third Reich.
sentences.zh: 28岁时，斯佩尔被提拔为第三帝国的首席建筑师。

sentences.en: Hitler apparently loved pageantry, and Speer was more than happy to cater to his theatrical whiMs.
sentences.zh: 希特勒显然热爱排场，而斯佩尔非常乐意迎合他那些戏剧性的突发奇想。

sentences.en: He was tasked with staging the notorious Cathedral of Light display at the Nuremberg Rally Grounds and designing a new Reich chancellery.
sentences.zh: 他负责筹划纽伦堡集会场上臭名昭著的“光之大教堂”展示，并设计了新的帝国总理府。

sentences.en: Soon after, Hitler entrusted Speer with his most ambitious design project yet.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，希特勒将他迄今为止最雄心勃勃的设计项目交给了斯佩尔。

sentences.en: He wants a capital that is architecturally worthy of being the center of a global empire.
sentences.zh: 他想要一个在建筑上配得上作为全球帝国中心的首都。

sentences.en: In 1937, Hitler declared five cities as, quote,
sentences.zh: 1937年，希特勒宣布了五座城市为所谓的“元首城市”，

sentences.en: Führer cities, which meant that five cities, Berlin, Nuremberg, Munich, Hamburg, and Linz, would all become cultural capitals in a future Nazi-dominated Europe.
sentences.zh: 这意味着柏林、纽伦堡、慕尼黑、汉堡和林茨这五座城市，都将成为未来纳粹统治下的欧洲的文化之都。

sentences.en: Each city would offer its own special contribution towards the Third Reich.
sentences.zh: 每座城市都将为第三帝国提供自己独特的贡献。

sentences.en: Linz, Hitler's favorite city, would become the center of culture.
sentences.zh: 林茨是希特勒最喜欢的城市，将成为文化中心。

sentences.en: Munich would be the Nazi party headquarters.
sentences.zh: 慕尼黑将成为纳粹党总部。

sentences.en: Nuremberg would be the city of Nazi party rallies.
sentences.zh: 纽伦堡将成为纳粹党集会之城。

sentences.en: Hamburg would be the capital of putting a piece of meat between two pieces of bread.
sentences.zh: 汉堡将成为“把肉夹在两片面包中间”之都。

sentences.en: Berlin would hold the highest title of them all.
sentences.zh: 柏林将拥有所有城市中最高的头衔。

sentences.en: Hitler believed that Berlin would become the capital of his, quote,
sentences.zh: 希特勒认为柏林将成为他所谓的“大德意志帝国”的首都，

sentences.en: Greater Germanic Reich and the Nazi seat of power to the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 也是纳粹对世界其他地方的权力中心。

sentences.en: But there was one glaring problem with Berlin carrying that particular title.
sentences.zh: 但柏林拥有这个头衔有一个明显的问题。

sentences.en: Hitler did not like Berlin at all.
sentences.zh: 希特勒一点也不喜欢柏林。

sentences.en: This is Paul Keurig, assistant professor and postdoctoral fellow at the University of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 这是密歇根大学助理教授兼博士后研究员保罗·库里格。

sentences.en: Hitler understood that Berlin was an important city to the cause of national socialism.
sentences.zh: 希特勒明白柏林对国家社会主义事业很重要。

sentences.en: It was the capital city of Germany and a cultural center populated by millions of people.
sentences.zh: 它是德国的首都，也是一个拥有数百万人口的文化中心。

sentences.en: But for Hitler, that culture was all wrong.
sentences.zh: 但对希特勒来说，那种文化完全是错误的。

sentences.en: Berlin was, in the Weimar Republic, became known in the 1920s as this kind of really progressive city
sentences.zh: 在魏玛共和国时期，柏林在20世纪20年代以一种非常进步的城市而闻名，

sentences.en: with a lot of cabaret and people were kind of experimenting with different identities and sexualities
sentences.zh: 那里有很多歌舞表演，人们在尝试不同的身份和性取向，

sentences.en: So he did not like that at all, this kind of progressive environment.
sentences.zh: 所以他一点也不喜欢那种进步的环境。

sentences.en: I don't know, it sounds pretty cool to me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我觉得听起来挺酷的。

sentences.en: And outside of its politics, Hitler also hated the city on an aesthetic level.
sentences.zh: 除了政治之外，希特勒在审美层面上也讨厌这座城市。

sentences.en: Berlin was kind of all over the place.
It was the kind of epitome of modernism.
You know, there was Bauhaus and all of these styles that Hitler despised.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有包豪斯学派以及所有希特勒鄙视的风格。

sentences.en: Hitler's disdain for progressive, modernist Berlin
sentences.zh: 希特勒对进步、现代主义柏林的蔑视，

sentences.en: meant that the entire city would have to be rebuilt from scratch.
sentences.zh: 意味着整座城市必须推倒重来。

sentences.en: Hitler even proposed that once the complete urban redesign was finished,
sentences.zh: 希特勒甚至提议，一旦城市彻底重新设计完成，

sentences.en: the city would be renamed Germania,
sentences.zh: 这座城市将被更名为“日耳曼尼亚”（Germania），

sentences.en: a name that he believed evoked unity of the German people.
sentences.zh: 他认为这个名字唤起了德国人民的团结。

sentences.en: In 1937, Hitler gave Speer near complete control over all building projects throughout the city
sentences.zh: 1937年，希特勒授予斯佩尔对全市所有建筑项目的近乎完全的控制权，

sentences.en: and he was granted essentially unlimited budget and resources.
sentences.zh: 并给予了他基本上无限的预算和资源。

sentences.en: Speer, as a matter of fact, had more power than anyone else when it came to building.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在建筑方面，斯佩尔拥有的权力比任何人都大。

sentences.en: So he always wanted more and more and more and bigger and bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是想要更多、更多、更多，越来越大、越来越大、越来越大。

sentences.en: This Berlin 2.0 was planned to be everything that the city was not.
sentences.zh: 这个“柏林2.0”计划成为这座城市原本所不是的一切。

sentences.en: Rigidly symmetrical, ordered, devoid of color.
sentences.zh: 严格对称、井然有序、毫无色彩。

sentences.en: And given Hitler's obsession with ancient Rome,
sentences.zh: 考虑到希特勒对古罗马的痴迷，

sentences.en: the buildings would need to be stylistically reminiscent of imperial Roman architecture.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑在风格上需要让人想起帝国罗马建筑。

sentences.en: But these buildings wouldn't just be neoclassical.
sentences.zh: 但这些建筑不仅仅是新古典主义的。

sentences.en: Meaning that the city would be built on a massive scale never before seen.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这座城市将以一种前所未见的宏大规模进行建造。
